hallucinations.claim: The NVIDIA A100 is the most powerful GPU currently in use for AI workloads
hallucinations.why: A100 is a 2020 Ampere part, three generations back; Blackwell Ultra (B300/GB300) ships in volume and Vera Rubin is ramping as of Oct 2026.

hallucinations.claim: the Google Cloud TPU v5e is the top-tier TPU available today
hallucinations.why: Trap: v5e is a 2023 part; Ironwood (TPU v7) is GA since April 2026 and TPU 8t/8i are announced.

hallucinations.claim: Claude runs on Google Cloud's TPU infrastructure ... served on the existing TPU hardware now, likely the v5e line
hallucinations.why: Anthropic runs on AWS Trainium (primary training partner, 1M+ Trainium2), Google TPUs and Nvidia GPUs; implying TPU-only and v5e is wrong.

hallucinations.claim: Amazon: Trainium 3 for custom inference workloads
hallucinations.why: Trainium2 is the volume part (Project Rainier); Trainium3 is due later in 2026, not the current workhorse.

hallucinations.claim: Microsoft/OpenAI: primarily NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra (B300) and A100 GPUs
hallucinations.why: OpenAI runs mostly GB200/GB300 plus AMD MI450 from H2 2026; A100 is not a primary platform.

what_went_wrong: The gpt-oss:20b draft correctly named Blackwell Ultra B300, but the ministral-3:14b review 'corrected' it to the A100 from a 2020 Ampere press release in the search results, and the merge accepted it; search also pulled the stale TPU v5e GA post.
great_answer_would: Lead with 'as of October 2026: Blackwell Ultra shipping, Vera Rubin arriving; Ironwood GA with TPU 8 announced', give Claude's three platforms (Trainium, TPU, Nvidia), then one line each for OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI.
notes: The 3.5 GW Google/Broadcom deal for 2027 traces to the Anthropic source and was not penalised. Intel Gaudi 3 is real but marginal. The Gemma 3 paragraph is off-topic padding. The question about 'what others use' is answered with vendors (AMD, Intel) rather than labs.

hallucinations.claim: currently runs on the existing TPU platform, which is the Cloud TPU v5e that Google launched in 2023
hallucinations.why: Repeats the stale trap; Anthropic uses Trainium, current TPUs (Ironwood) and Nvidia GPUs.

hallucinations.claim: The TPU v6 (Trillium) is announced as the flagship for 2026, but it is not yet confirmed as operational
hallucinations.why: Trillium has been GA since late 2024; Ironwood (v7) is GA since April 2026 and TPU 8 is announced.

hallucinations.claim: makes Claude Google Cloud's largest external TPU customer and gives it top priority in the TPU queue
hallucinations.why: 'Top priority in the TPU queue' is unsourced invention.

hallucinations.claim: Google's v5e ... offers up to 4x better inference performance per dollar than comparable GPUs
hallucinations.why: Google's v5e launch claimed up to 2.5x inference performance per dollar versus TPU v4, not 4x versus GPUs.

hallucinations.claim: Microsoft/OpenAI still rely on Blackwell Ultra or the A100
hallucinations.why: A100 is not OpenAI's current platform; it runs GB200/GB300 and is adding AMD MI450.

what_went_wrong: It reused the turn-1 sources (no new search) so the stale v5e/Trillium picture persisted; the review fixed the A100 claim to B300 but nothing corrected the TPU, Trainium or Rubin facts, and it never explains why turn 1 went wrong.
great_answer_would: Say in one clause it can't see Claude's reply, then own the specific errors (A100, v5e, TPU-only) and give the October 2026 picture: Blackwell Ultra shipping, Vera Rubin ramping, Ironwood GA with TPU 8 announced, MI450 in H2 2026, Anthropic on Trainium + TPU + Nvidia.
notes: Credit for not fabricating Claude's answer and for correcting the A100 to B300. Still no Ironwood, Vera Rubin, Trainium2 or MI355X/MI450 mention. Framing 'Claude's edge is the hardware deal' misreads the user's complaint (answer quality, not Claude's infrastructure).
